column3: “Went … to drink” is rendered “came to drink wine.”
“At the feast of wine” is rendered “as they drank their wine at the banquet.”

“To male slaves and to female slaves” is rendered “as slaves, men and women.” The last clause is difficult; NASB renders it “the trouble would not be commensurate with the annoyance to the king,” and the meaning is uncertain.
The Hebrew repeats “he said”; NASB has “asked.” “Whose heart has filled him” is rendered “who would presume.”
“The feast of wine” is rendered “drinking wine”; NASB supplies “went.”
“The house of the feast of wine” is rendered “the place where they were drinking wine,” and “violate” as “assault.”
NASB spells “Harbonah.” “Who spoke good on the king” is rendered “who spoke good on behalf of the king.”
